title: Integrating Innovation and Responsibility in Sustainable Farming Practices
source: Proceedings of The World Conference on Business Management and Economics
summary: The agri-food sector is facing unprecedented challenges in the 21st century, characterised by interlinked geopolitical, demographic, environmental and technological factors that require innovative solutions with sustainability principles in
content: The agri-food sector is facing unprecedented challenges in the 21st century, characterised by interlinked geopolitical, demographic, environmental and technological factors that require innovative solutions with sustainability principles in mind. Climate change, deteriorating natural resources and the need to ensure food security for a growing world population are forcing managers to reflect on these challenges. Responsible innovative approaches can significantly reduce the negative impact on the environment while maintaining or improving the level of productivity that is essential for future development. These innovative approaches to business management must be based on quality management, learning and the transfer of new knowledge and skills into practice. Digital technologies, precision farming and smart management systems are key innovations in addressing the challenges of climate change and food security concerns. The primary objective of the scientific paper is to identify current global challenges and trends in the sustainability of the agricultural sector and to evaluate the effectiveness of innovative technological solutions in transforming sustainable farm management practices, with particular focus on comparing the Slovak and EU agricultural sectors' adoption rates. Through a comprehensive analysis of longitudinal data (2018-2024), this research investigates the relation between technological integration and environmental sustainability metrics in the Slovak agricultural sector, compared with broader European Union benchmarks. The findings indicate a significant positive relation between innovation adoption rates and agricultural sustainability metrics. The research question of the article is whether the integration of innovative technological solutions in Slovak agricultural enterprises has a positive relationship with improved sustainability performance metrics.

title: A high-resolution methodology for mapping and predicting salt marsh dynamics: integrating LiDAR data and spatiotemporal varying tidal datums
source: Ecological Informatics
summary: Accurate assessment of salt marsh dynamics is crucial to reverse their widespread decline. Previous modelling studies investigated the resilience to mean sea level rise, ignoring the tidal dynamics observed in many estuaries. Building on th
content: Accurate assessment of salt marsh dynamics is crucial to reverse their widespread decline. Previous modelling studies investigated the resilience to mean sea level rise, ignoring the tidal dynamics observed in many estuaries. Building on the principle that salt marsh occurrence is determined by soil elevation relative to tidal datums, this study aims to map the current extent of salt marshes and project their long-term evolution by combining high-resolution LiDAR data with spatially varying tidal datums. The Ria de Aveiro, a lagoon undergoing tidal amplification, was used as a case study. A simplified, rule-based model of long-term marsh evolution was developed, in which vertical accretion is derived endogenously as a function of tidal datums. It was validated in hindcast mode by reconstructing the 1987 marsh extent, and applied to project marsh dynamics to 2100. A Monte Carlo analysis quantified the projection uncertainty and disentangled the influence of accretion from that of the datum variability. The soil elevation–datum relationship proved effective for mapping, yielding an overall accuracy of 90.3%. The model reproduced the 1987 extent and captured a 26% decline in marsh area between 1987 and 2024 (from 34.8 to 25.7 km 2 ). This decline is projected to continue through 2100, reaching a median area of 17.5 km 2 , partly due to anthropogenic barriers that impede landward migration. The projected area is controlled by accretion, with datum variability becoming decisive in the inner regions. Future research should apply this model to other estuarine systems, especially those with salt marshes threatened by tidal amplification.

title: The Scope 3 Data Dilemma: How Much Real Data Makes a Product Footprint Credible?
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Code, data and figures for a reproducible EU-27 benchmark of tier-by-tier product carbon footprint (PCF) chaining under partial supply-chain participation. An emissions-extended input-output model of the EU-27 economy is built from two open
content: Code, data and figures for a reproducible EU-27 benchmark of tier-by-tier product carbon footprint (PCF) chaining under partial supply-chain participation. An emissions-extended input-output model of the EU-27 economy is built from two open Eurostat datasets (naio_10_cp1750 symmetric input-output table and env_ac_ainah_r2 air emissions accounts, reference year 2022); because the full network is observed, the true cradle-to-gate footprint of every industry is exactly computable and used as ground truth. PACT/Catena-X-style footprint chaining is simulated at every level of supply-chain participation and scored on impact error, uncertainty calibration and ranking stability. The full 3,840-condition grid reproduces end to end in under two minutes with no commercial license.

title: Digital Twins in the Architectural Design Stage for Sustainable Net-Zero Buildings: A Systematic Review of Frameworks, Tools, and Research Gaps
source: Open Science Framework
summary: This project presents a systematic review titled “Digital Twins in the Architectural Design Stage for Sustainable Net-Zero Buildings: A Systematic Review of Frameworks, Tools, and Research Gaps.” Its purpose is to examine how digital twin t
content: This project presents a systematic review titled “Digital Twins in the Architectural Design Stage for Sustainable Net-Zero Buildings: A Systematic Review of Frameworks, Tools, and Research Gaps.” Its purpose is to examine how digital twin technologies are being conceptualised, developed and applied during the architectural design stage to support net-zero building performance. The project focuses particularly on concept and schematic design, when decisions concerning building form, orientation, spatial configuration, envelope, glazing, materials and passive strategies remain flexible and can significantly influence subsequent energy use, operational emissions and embodied carbon. Although digital twins are increasingly used in the architecture, engineering and construction sector, most established applications relate to construction, building operation, monitoring, maintenance and facility management. Their role in early architectural design remains comparatively unclear and underdeveloped. In particular, many studies use the term “digital twin” for BIM-based simulations, parametric models or performance-analysis workflows without demonstrating the dynamic data connections, feedback mechanisms and decision-support capabilities normally associated with a mature digital twin. This project therefore investigates whether existing design-stage digital twins function as genuine decision-support systems or remain fragmented BIM-plus-simulation workflows carrying a digital-twin label. The review is guided by five research questions: How are digital twins defined and conceptualised in studies relating to the architectural design stage? What types of digital twin frameworks have been proposed to support architectural design decisions? Which tools, platforms and enabling technologies are used in design-stage digital twin workflows? Which net-zero performance indicators are addressed by existing design-stage digital twin studies? What technical, methodological and practical gaps limit the adoption of digital twins in architectural net-zero design? The review follows the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework and combines systematic screening with descriptive content analysis, thematic synthesis and a structured maturity appraisal. A review protocol defining the research questions, search strategy, eligibility criteria, data-extraction template and appraisal method was prepared before screening. Searches were undertaken between 2 and 28 March 2026 in six bibliographic databases: Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink and Taylor & Francis Online. The search strategy combined terms relating to digital twins, the architectural design stage, net-zero or low-carbon buildings, and relevant tools or performance-analysis methods. The searches and citation tracking identified 159 records. title: Climate Justice Through Environmental Rights In the GCC Region: A Case Study of the State of Qatar: Status, Critique and Alternatives
source: SOAS Research Online (SOAS University of London)
summary: In the context of the increasingly urgent issues of climate change facing the world, the aim of this thesis is to assess the legal framework required to tackle these issues in the fossil fuel dependent countries of the Gulf Co-operation Cou
content: In the context of the increasingly urgent issues of climate change facing the world, the aim of this thesis is to assess the legal framework required to tackle these issues in the fossil fuel dependent countries of the Gulf Co-operation Council (GCC). It will be argued that the legal framework constructed to respond to climate change risks should integrate the principles of justice, fairness, and equity. The thesis will provide an in-depth evaluation of the inclusivity of decision-making processes related to climate change adaptation and mitigation measures, and the extent to which these processes achieve distributional justice in balancing the harms and benefits of emissions. By evaluating the legal framework through the lens of distributional justice, procedural justice, corrective justice, and social justice, this thesis will attempt to provide a conceptual framing for the GCC region to draft laws which respond to climate change and address the challenges of transitioning to a low-carbon economy.

title: Replication Package for Do Gender-Inclusive Economies Build More Sustainable Logistics Systems? Cross-Country Evidence on Logistics Performance and Transport Carbon Intensity
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository contains the data, code, documentation, and replication materials supporting the study “Do Gender-Inclusive Economies Build More Sustainable Logistics Systems? Cross-Country Evidence on Logistics Performance and Transport Ca
content: This repository contains the data, code, documentation, and replication materials supporting the study “Do Gender-Inclusive Economies Build More Sustainable Logistics Systems? Cross-Country Evidence on Logistics Performance and Transport Carbon Intensity.” The study examines whether gender-inclusive labor-market participation is associated with national logistics performance and transport carbon intensity using longitudinal cross-country data covering seven historical editions of the World Bank Logistics Performance Index (LPI). The analysis integrates publicly available indicators from the World Bank, ILOSTAT, and EDGAR/JRC-derived sources. The replication package includes frozen processed analytical datasets, a public-source data downloader, deterministic preprocessing code, Python analysis and verification scripts, a detailed codebook, source register, country-universe and country-wave inclusion documentation, expected statistical outputs, and figures used in the study. These materials are intended to support transparent verification and reproducibility of the reported analyses, tables, and figures. The archived processed data represent the analytical snapshot used for the study and were extracted on 20 August 2026. Because public data providers may subsequently revise historical observations, the archived datasets should be used for exact numerical replication of the published results. The study uses aggregated, publicly available country-level indicators and contains no individual-level or personally identifiable data.

title: Omnichannel Logistics
source: OpenAlex 学术文献
summary: In this chapter, we explore the evolution of omnichannel logistics, tracing the shift from siloed multichannel approaches to an integrated, customer-centric strategy. We examine the two components of omnichannel logistics, retailing and ful
content: In this chapter, we explore the evolution of omnichannel logistics, tracing the shift from siloed multichannel approaches to an integrated, customer-centric strategy. We examine the two components of omnichannel logistics, retailing and fulfillment, to demonstrate how boundaries between physical and digital commerce are blurring. We explain several fulfillment modes, including buy-online-ship-to-store (BOSS), direct-to-consumer (D2C), and buy-online-pick-up-in-store (BOPIS), and emphasize the critical role of real-time visibility and strategic inventory placement to minimize costs while maximizing service levels. Furthermore, we investigate future developments in the sector, highlighting the transformative impact of artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and the emergence of seamless “phygital” experiences. We assess the environmental sustainability challenges inherent in these complex networks, such as increased carbon emissions from last-mile delivery, packaging waste, and the ecological footprint of reverse logistics. We conclude by advocating for a holistic ecosystem approach that balances escalating consumer demands for convenience with operational efficiency and environmental responsibility. Omnichannel is focused on breaking down silos between channels and fulfillment modes and will require navigating trade-offs among economic, ecological, and social considerations in the future.

title: Sustainable Energy Systems
source: OpenAlex 学术文献
summary: This Reprint presents recent advances in sustainable energy systems and explores their progress, challenges, and future prospects in the context of global decarbonization and energy transition. The collected papers cover a broad range of to
content: This Reprint presents recent advances in sustainable energy systems and explores their progress, challenges, and future prospects in the context of global decarbonization and energy transition. The collected papers cover a broad range of topics, including renewable energy technologies, hydrogen development, low-carbon transportation, smart buildings, integrated energy systems, energy security, and digital innovations for energy management. The contributions highlight how technological innovation, system optimization, policy design, and international cooperation can jointly support the transition toward sustainable and resilient energy systems. By combining engineering research, economic assessment, and governance analysis, this Reprint provides a comprehensive perspective on the opportunities and challenges facing energy systems in an era of carbon neutrality.The Reprint serves as a valuable resource for researchers, policymakers, industry practitioners, and graduate students interested in sustainable energy development and long-term energy transition pathways.

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Low-Emission Methane Tri-Reforming: Carbon Formation, Hydrogen Production, and Operating-Window Optimization
source: ChemRxiv
summary: Tri-reforming of methane (TRM) is a promising route for producing hydrogen-rich syngas while partially utilizing CO2, but its deployment is limited by trade-offs among methane conversion, syngas composition, reactor duty, and carbon deposit
content: Tri-reforming of methane (TRM) is a promising route for producing hydrogen-rich syngas while partially utilizing CO2, but its deployment is limited by trade-offs among methane conversion, syngas composition, reactor duty, and carbon deposition. In this study, a Gibbsequilibrium model in Aspen Plus was used to generate a database of 46,464 operating points spanning temperature, pressure, and inlet H2O/CH4, CO2/CH4, and O2/CH4 ratios. Decision tree, random forest, XGBoost, and artificial neural network models were trained and compared, followed by SHAP and permutation-importance analysis and multi-objective genetic-algorithm optimization. The neural network showed the best predictive performance. Explainability analysis identified temperature as the dominant factor governing carbon formation, followed by steam, carbon dioxide, and oxygen feed ratios. Optimization revealed multiple distinct operating windows, confirming that no single universal optimum exists and demonstrating a rapid, interpretable framework for low-emission TRM screening and design.

title: Ecological integration protection and social welfare: evidence from China’s Shan-Shui initiative
source: Frontiers in Environmental Science
summary: Social welfare improvement, which integrates the enhancement of residents’ living quality and the realization of social equity, is the core goal of ecological integration protection and regional development. It is of great significance to p
content: Social welfare improvement, which integrates the enhancement of residents’ living quality and the realization of social equity, is the core goal of ecological integration protection and regional development. It is of great significance to promote the sustainable development of county areas. As a systematic ecological governance initiative, China’s Shan-Shui Initiative (SSI) serves as an innovative measure to promote the coordinated development of ecological governance, economic progress and improvement of social welfare. Based on panel data of county level regions in China from 2011 to 2023, this study evaluates the level of social welfare from three dimensions: economic development level, people’s livelihood security level, and economic structure optimization level. The difference-in-differences method is used to analyze the impact of SSI on county-level social welfare in China. The results show that: (1) SSI significantly promotes the improvement of social welfare, which has been tested by robustness. (2) The mechanism analysis reveals that SSI can advance urbanization and strengthen government environmental governance intensity, and then promote social welfare improvement. (3) The impact of SSI on social welfare is heterogeneous, with the most pronounced effects observed in central China and regions with moderate marketization levels. This study provides new evidence on how ecological integration protection affects social welfare, and offers theoretical and policy insights for advancing human-nature harmony in the new development stage.

title: Reconstructed VOC emissions reveal hidden ozone precursors: Overlooked roles of primary OVOCs and unmeasured species
source: Atmospheric chemistry and physics
summary: Abstract. Ambient volatile organic compounds (VOCs), including non-methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) and oxygenated VOCs (OVOCs), are critical precursors of tropospheric ozone (O3). However, conventional estimates of the ozone formation potentia
content: Abstract. Ambient volatile organic compounds (VOCs), including non-methane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) and oxygenated VOCs (OVOCs), are critical precursors of tropospheric ozone (O3). However, conventional estimates of the ozone formation potential (OFP) derived from observed VOC concentrations may introduce substantial biases, as they neglect the photochemical degradation of primary VOCs and the concurrent generation of secondary OVOCs during atmospheric transport. This study quantified the sources of ambient OVOCs at a suburban site in Shanghai, China during summer 2020 to reconstruct their initial emission concentrations. Together with the reconstructed initial concentrations of NMHCs, we estimated the OFP of freshly emitted VOCs. In addition, the sources and the OFP of unmeasured VOCs were inferred by concurrent measurements of missing OH reactivity. Our results demonstrate that photochemical reactions substantially altered the composition and source characteristics of VOCs, leading to pronounced discrepancies in the OFP estimation between observed and reconstructed initial concentrations. Specifically, the OFP contributions from reconstructed primary emitted NMHCs (52.3 %) were underestimated by 31.7 % when derived from observed concentrations for this site, whereas those from reconstructed primary emitted OVOCs (33.2 %) were overestimated by 42.6 %. Reconstructed VOC emissions indicated that anthropogenic sources dominated total emissions (71.5 %), whereas OVOCs constituted a substantial fraction of total VOC emissions (40.8 %). Unmeasured VOCs, primarily of biogenic origin, contributed an additional 12.6 %. Collectively, OVOCs and unmeasured species exhibited an OFP comparable to NMHCs, underscoring their critical role in O3 production and the necessity of incorporating these species into the design of comprehensive and effective O3 control strategies.

title: Emissive BN‐Embedded Cumulenes: Synthesis and Bidirectional Photocurrent Modulation
source: Angewandte Chemie
summary: ABSTRACT Embedding boron and nitrogen (BN) units into π‐conjugated frameworks provides an effective strategy to tune electronic structures by introducing intrinsic orbital polarization arising from the vacant p orbital of boron and the lone
content: ABSTRACT Embedding boron and nitrogen (BN) units into π‐conjugated frameworks provides an effective strategy to tune electronic structures by introducing intrinsic orbital polarization arising from the vacant p orbital of boron and the lone pair of nitrogen. While BN‐embedding has been extensively explored in C(sp 2 ) polyaromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), its impact on the optoelectronic properties of C(sp)‐rich systems remains underexplored. Here we report air‐ and moisture‐stable BN‐capped sp‐carbon chains that are isoelectronic to [3]‐ and [5]cumulenes ( [n]BN , n = 3, 5). Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal that BN‐embedding induces pronounced polarization and localizes the high‐frequency skeletal vibrations. Consequently, [n]BN exhibit excimer‐like solid‐state fluorescence, whereas the all‐carbon counterparts remain weakly or non‐emissive. Leveraging the characteristics of excited‐state charge separation and asymmetric carrier injection, heterojunction optoelectronic devices incorporating [3]BN display unique bidirectional photocurrent modulation, establishing BN‐embedding as an effective strategy to tune the electronic structure and emergent functions of C(sp)‐rich systems.

title: Interactive effects of a fermented organic extract (eco-enzyme) and balanced organic substrate on flowering of geranium (Pelargonium hortorum)
source: Journal of Ecological Engineering
summary: Container-grown geranium (Pelargonium hortorum) may experience delayed flowering and leaf chlorosis due to limited nutrient availability and a high carbon-to-nitrogen ratio in the growing medium.Optimizing substrate composition together wit
content: Container-grown geranium (Pelargonium hortorum) may experience delayed flowering and leaf chlorosis due to limited nutrient availability and a high carbon-to-nitrogen ratio in the growing medium.Optimizing substrate composition together with biostimulant application may therefore improve both flowering performance and ornamental quality.However, the interactive effects of eco-enzyme application and organic growing media formulation on geranium flowering remain unexplored.This study assessed the interactive effects of eco-enzyme concentration and organic growing media composition on the flowering performance of geranium.A factorial randomized block design was used, evaluating three eco-enzyme concentrations (0, 15, and 30 mL L⁻¹) and three media formulations composed of cocopeat, manure, and rice husk biochar (1:1:0, 1:1:1, and 1:1:2).The M2 medium (1:1:1) was well balanced, with favorable bulk density, porosity, and water-holding capacity that supported root development and nutrient uptake.Eco-enzyme application at 15-30 mL L⁻¹ significantly (P < 0.05) increased flower cluster number by 31.1-59.0% in the M2 medium compared to untreated plants.The M2 medium increased flower number and cluster diameter by 18.9% and 6.3%, respectively, compared to the M3 (1:1:2) formulation, while 30 mL L⁻¹ eco-enzyme increased flower number by 25.8% compared to the control.These combined effects promoted earlier, fuller flowering and greater plant vigor.Incorporating eco-enzyme biostimulant application with an optimized organic substrate therefore offers a practical and sustainable strategy to enhance geranium flowering performance and ornamental quality.

title: Virtual Preoperative Education in Bariatric Surgery: Patient Acceptance and Travel-Related Carbon Savings
source: Obesity Surgery
summary: BACKGROUND: Comprehensive preoperative patient education is critical for optimizing postoperative outcomes and long-term weight management after bariatric surgery. Traditional in-person educational sessions, however, generate considerable g
content: BACKGROUND: Comprehensive preoperative patient education is critical for optimizing postoperative outcomes and long-term weight management after bariatric surgery. Traditional in-person educational sessions, however, generate considerable greenhouse gas emissions, primarily due to participant travel. Telemedicine offers an environmentally sustainable alternative with the potential to reduce the carbon footprint within obesity care. This study aimed to quantify savings in greenhouse gas emissions and assess patient acceptance of virtual preoperative obesity educational sessions compared to conventional in-person courses. METHODS: Between January and December 2024, N = 183 patients attending a virtual preoperative educational seminar for individuals with obesity-integrated into standard bariatric surgical preparation-were surveyed regarding their hypothetical travel behavior, had the seminar been held in person. Distances from participants' residences to the seminar location and preferred transportation modes were used to calculate avoided CO₂ emissions utilizing the Transport Emission Model (TREMOD) developed by the German Federal Environment Agency. RESULTS: The average one-way travel distance was 33.08 km, with 83.6% of participants indicating they would have traveled by private vehicle, predominantly powered by internal combustion engines. Transitioning to the virtual format resulted in a total avoidance of approximately 1.792 metric tons of CO₂ equivalent emissions over the study period. Patient acceptance of the virtual format was high, with 93.4% of the cohort rating it as equivalent or superior to in-person sessions. Notably, 25% of the participants stated they would not have attended the mandatory session if held exclusively in person, indicating that the virtual format successfully bridged a significant attendance gap. CONCLUSIONS: Given the increasing prevalence of obesity and the critical role of preoperative education in bariatric care, telemedicine represents an effective strategy to meaningfully reduce travel-related emissions. Virtual educational interventions eliminate CO₂-intensive journeys while maintaining broad accessibility and high patient satisfaction. Integrating telemedicine into obesity surgery care pathways can thus significantly contribute to sustainable, climate-conscious healthcare delivery.

title: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) Data Package
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) Data Package This dataset provides comprehensive information on the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), compiled from the EU Transaction Log (EUTL) and related public sources. It covers ins
content: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) Data Package This dataset provides comprehensive information on the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS), compiled from the EU Transaction Log (EUTL) and related public sources. It covers installations regulated under the EU ETS, including their compliance records (verified emissions, allocations, surrendered allowances), registry accounts and account holders, unit-level transactions, and CDM/JI offset projects. Complementary tables provide geocoded installation coordinates, NACE economic activity codes derived from the EU carbon leakage lists, and EUA primary auction prices and volumes from the European Energy Exchange (EEX). The data are published as a Frictionless Data Package containing interlinked CSV tables with a full schema descriptor. All tables are sourced from publicly available data; the underlying records remain the property of their respective providers (European Commission, EEX, Eurostat) and are subject to those providers' reuse terms. The CC-BY-4.0 license covers the compilation, structuring, and transformations contributed by the authors. The processing code used to generate this dataset is available at https://jabrell.github.io/euetsinfo/. Version 2: Added links to ENTSOE power plants and industrial facilities reporting under the Industrial Emission Directive

title: The Linkages Between Factors of the Transport Environment: An Evaluation of the Capacity, Network and Environment Related Aspects
source: Journal of Transportation and Logistics
summary: The transport environment---which includes network, capacity, and climate change factors---becomes increasingly important with the growing integration and competition among complex supply chain networks and the boom in e-commerce. However,
content: The transport environment---which includes network, capacity, and climate change factors---becomes increasingly important with the growing integration and competition among complex supply chain networks and the boom in e-commerce. However, research on transport mainly examines factors from the macroenvironment, leading to findings that are applicable to a general context. Further research is necessary for a thorough understanding, particularly of the relationships among the components of the transport environment. To fill this gap, the objective of this study is to analyze the association between various elements of the transport environment, including capacity, network, and environment-related aspects. A panel Granger causality investigation is conducted on the variables, including container transport, freight transport, road and rail density, and transport CO2 (carbon dioxide) emissions for G7 (Group of Seven) countries from 1994 to 2018. The results emphasize the significance of transport modes in decarbonizing the sector. The findings also highlight that maritime and road transport are primary areas to be tackled on the path to net-zero emissions. As a promising mode for emission reduction, transport policy should prioritize rail transport in the context of the green transition. Moreover, the supply of rail networks should be in line with the rail freight demand.

title: Climate change and food security in sustainable finance: a South African perspective
source: Frontiers in Climate
summary: In South Africa, climate change is increasingly threatening food security through droughts, irregular rainfall, high temperatures, floods, water shortage and reduced agricultural productivity. This study conducted a systematic review of Sou
content: In South Africa, climate change is increasingly threatening food security through droughts, irregular rainfall, high temperatures, floods, water shortage and reduced agricultural productivity. This study conducted a systematic review of South African studies on the integration of climate change, food security and sustainable finance. The review was implemented using Climate-Resilient Food Systems Framework and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The review process involved identifying 173 documents from Scopus, Web of Science, Science Direct and Google Scholar, among which 37 articles were selected for the final synthesis. Results indicate that the available data comprehensively report climate change effects on agriculture, livelihoods and household food security with a focus on smallholder farmers. Nevertheless, the integration of sustainable finance into the food security and adaptation research is still very limited. Public investment, agricultural credit, green finance, climate finance, extension-linked support, and digital finance were identified as key yet disconnected mechanisms for enhancing resilience. The main obstacles are financial exclusion, poor institutional capacity, lack of coordination, insufficient climate information, poor infrastructure, and socio-economic vulnerability. This systematic review contributes to the literature by developing an integrated evidence-based conceptual framework for climate change, sustainable finance, adaptation, and food security. The study recommends that policymakers, financial institutions, and development practitioners adopt the proposed integrated conceptual framework to guide the design of climate-resilient food-system policies, sustainable finance strategies, and adaptation interventions.

title: Institutional Quality, Energy Transition and Environmental Sustainability in CIS Countries: Panel Evidence for SDG13
source: Economies
summary: This study investigates how institutional quality conditions the relationship between energy transition and environmental sustainability in nine CIS economies over the period 1996–2024, drawing on annual panel data sourced from the World De
content: This study investigates how institutional quality conditions the relationship between energy transition and environmental sustainability in nine CIS economies over the period 1996–2024, drawing on annual panel data sourced from the World Development Indicators. In the empirical framework, carbon dioxide emissions are specified as the dependent variable, while industrial output, foreign direct investment (FDI), renewable energy consumption, economic growth, trade openness, overall energy use, and an institutional quality index are included as key determinants of environmental pressure. Methodologically, the paper employs second-generation panel econometric techniques, commencing with cross-sectional dependence diagnostics and panel unit root tests, and proceeding to long-run estimation through FMOLS and CCR. The robustness of these estimates is reinforced using Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, while the System-GMM estimator is applied to address heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, cross-sectional dependence, and endogeneity concerns. The results indicate that industrial activity, energy consumption, and FDI significantly increase CO2 emissions, whereas greater reliance on renewable energy and stronger institutional quality help to alleviate environmental degradation. Under more rigorous specifications, trade openness and economic growth are found to reduce emissions, pointing to emerging decoupling patterns within CIS countries. Importantly, the interaction between renewable energy and institutional quality reveals a pronounced complementary effect, suggesting that stronger governance frameworks amplify the environmental benefits of energy transition. Taken together, the findings underscore that environmental sustainability across CIS economies is jointly determined by structural, economic, and institutional factors, with institutional quality serving as a critical lever for advancing progress toward SDG 13.

title: Editorial: Gas hydrates in Arctic and permafrost regions special issue
source: Environmental Geotechnics
summary: The Arctic regions of the Earth, including the Arctic continental shelf, are among the most promising and actively developed areas. This is primarily due to the abundance of natural resources, including major oil and gas reserves as well as
content: The Arctic regions of the Earth, including the Arctic continental shelf, are among the most promising and actively developed areas. This is primarily due to the abundance of natural resources, including major oil and gas reserves as well as significant deposits of metallic mineral resources. New transportation corridors are of particular importance in the Arctic, most notably the Northern Sea Route connecting Southeast Asia with Western Europe, as well as port infrastructure facilities located along the coasts of the Arctic seas. However, the development of the Arctic regions is complicated by a number of factors, including the harsh climate, unique permafrost and geological conditions, challenging logistics, and other environmental and infrastructural constraints. The presence of permafrost represents a major geotechnical challenge for the construction and long-term operation of engineering structures and infrastructure facilities. A serious source of geological risk in the development of Arctic regions is represented by natural gas hydrate accumulations. In the Arctic, these geological formations are mainly associated with the formation and evolution of the cryolithozone, driven by global climatic changes on Earth. The widespread occurrence of permafrost in Arctic regions and its considerable thickness, reaching several hundred meters, create favourable thermobaric conditions for gas hydrate accumulation over a wide interval of the geological section, both onshore and within the Arctic shelf. As a result, many shallow gas reservoirs located beneath permafrost may be converted into the gas hydrate state, while permafrost sequences can act as an effective caprock, promoting the accumulation of natural gas in the form of gas hydrates supplied from the Earth’s interior during degassing processes. Large gas hydrate accumulations occurring above conventional hydrocarbon reservoirs in the Arctic are considered promising targets for future development as currently exploited gas fields become progressively depleted.Particular attention is currently being paid to permafrost degradation processes in the Arctic associated with global climate change. This issue is also highly relevant to the Arctic shelf, where relic subsea permafrost, formed during earlier periods of subaerial exposure, is widespread. Permafrost degradation leads to the destabilization of both intrapermafrost and subpermafrost gas hydrate accumulations. This, in turn, results in the intensification of gas-dynamic processes within rock sequences and promotes active methane emissions both on the Arctic shelf and onshore. In recent years, numerous methane seep sites have been identified on the Arctic shelf. According to a number of researchers, these features are associated with the degradation of subsea permafrost and the dissociation of gas hydrates. title: Green manuring promotes sustainable soil management in bangladesh through agronomic benefits mechanisms and global perspectives
source: Discover Agriculture
summary: Green manuring (GM) is an important ecological approach for restoring soil fertility and promoting sustainable agriculture, particularly in regions experiencing soil degradation and intensive cropping systems. Bangladesh faces severe soil f
content: Green manuring (GM) is an important ecological approach for restoring soil fertility and promoting sustainable agriculture, particularly in regions experiencing soil degradation and intensive cropping systems. Bangladesh faces severe soil fertility decline due to continuous rice-based cultivation, excessive use of chemical fertilizers, and reduced organic matter levels. This review synthesizes current knowledge on green manuring practices in Bangladesh while integrating global research insights on its role in improving soil health and agricultural sustainability. Leguminous green manuring crops such as Sesbania rostrata , Sesbania aculeata , Crotalaria juncea , Vigna unguiculata , and Vigna radiata can fix approximately 50 to 250 kg N ha −1 through symbiotic interactions with rhizobia, significantly reducing the need for synthetic fertilizers. In addition to biological N fixations, both leguminous and non-leguminous green manure species enhance soil organic matter, improve soil structure, stimulate microbial activity, and increase nutrient cycling. Evidence from field studies indicates that integrating green manures into rice-based cropping systems can increase crop yields by 15 to 45% while improving soil carbon sequestration and nutrient availability. Green manuring also contributes to climate-smart agriculture by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, enhancing soil water retention, and mitigating soil salinity and erosion in vulnerable agroecosystems. Despite these benefits, the adoption of green manuring in Bangladesh remains limited due to insufficient farmer awareness, inadequate seed supply systems, and short-term economic constraints. Strengthening, extension services, developing reliable seed systems, and incorporating green manuring into national soil fertility management policies are essential for wider adoption. In conclusion, green manuring represents a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable strategy to restore soil health, improve crop productivity, and enhance climate resilience in Bangladesh and similar agroecological regions worldwide.

title: Hydrogeochemistry and water management in a Venezuelan heavy oil reservoir: Evidence from the Carabobo field
source: Physics and Chemistry of the Earth Parts A/B/C
summary: To understand the origin and evolution of formation waters in the Carabobo oil reservoirs, a hydrogeochemical characterization was conducted on 73 water samples collected from production boreholes, rivers, aquifers, and drilling mud. Since
content: To understand the origin and evolution of formation waters in the Carabobo oil reservoirs, a hydrogeochemical characterization was conducted on 73 water samples collected from production boreholes, rivers, aquifers, and drilling mud. Since the oil boreholes were active, the local effects on them were considered beforehand, to diagnose water-related problems. The primary objective of this study was to demonstrate how data from a regional investigation can be used to improve the understanding of local water-related issues and optimize oil production management, while simultaneously refining the outcomes of the regional assessment. At the local scale, chemical and isotopic analyses revealed water intrusion from an upper stratum in one borehole, pipe corrosion in another, and methanogenesis in most boreholes. Notably, a deuterium enrichment in water (exceeding +10‰ δD relative to the meteoric water line) resulting from methanogenic activity under isolated conditions was documented. This study demonstrates the potential of hydrogeochemistry as a tool for systematically characterizing oilfield waters. It reveals how water interacts with porous media, organic matter, and microorganisms, as evidenced by their chemical and isotope compositions. This information is useful for optimizing oil reservoir management and promoting the oil production.

title: First comparison of XCO <sub>2</sub> products from DQ-1 ACDL and passive optical satellites
source: OpenAlex 学术文献
summary: Abstract. Spaceborne active CO2 IPDA lidar provides an active remote-sensing approach for XCO2 observations that differs from passive NIR/SWIR remote sensing. However, comparisons between DQ-1 ACDL and passive optical satellite XCO2 product
content: Abstract. Spaceborne active CO2 IPDA lidar provides an active remote-sensing approach for XCO2 observations that differs from passive NIR/SWIR remote sensing. However, comparisons between DQ-1 ACDL and passive optical satellite XCO2 products remain limited. Here we compare DQ-1 ACDL with OCO-2, OCO-3, GOSAT, and GOSAT-2 XCO2 products from June 2022 to December 2024 using a unified framework that combines CAMS-based spatiotemporal coherence assessment, satellite sampling availability, daily 2° aggregation, spatiotemporal collocation, and XCO2 column-definition correction. The results show that DQ-1 is broadly consistent with OCO-2 and OCO-3 over coherent and well-sampled regions, with mean differences mostly below 0.5 ppm and similar spatial distributions, meridional structures, and regional monthly variations. Nighttime DQ-1 XCO2 is also consistent with CAMS-derived XCO2, indicating stable performance relative to an external model reference. Independent validation against TCCON shows that daytime DQ-1 XCO2 has a correlation coefficient of 0.92, a mean bias of 0.21 ppm, and an RMSE of 1.49 ppm, with statistics comparable to GOSAT. Regional results further indicate that DQ-1 does not simply duplicate existing passive satellite observations, but provides complementary XCO2 observational coverage under high aerosol loading, at high latitudes, and in regions where passive observations are limited. Overall, DQ-1 ACDL is comparable to passive satellite XCO2 products under the unified framework, and can serve as an important complement to existing passive satellite XCO2 observations, supporting future active–passive joint XCO2 constraints, regional carbon flux inversions, and emission monitoring.

title: Board Diversity, Sustainability Committee, And Environmental Performance As Determinants Of Carbon Emission Disclosure: Evidence From Indonesian Listed Companies
source: The Indonesian Accounting Review
summary: This study examines the determinants of carbon emission disclosure among non-financial companies listed in the Top 100 Capitalization market on the Indonesian Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period. While prior research has yielde
content: This study examines the determinants of carbon emission disclosure among non-financial companies listed in the Top 100 Capitalization market on the Indonesian Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period. While prior research has yielded mixed findings on the relationship between board characteristics and carbon disclosure, limited evidence exists in the Indonesian context, particularly regarding the combined effects of board diversity, sustainability committees, and environmental performance. Drawing on Stakeholder Theory, Legitimacy Theory, Agency Theory, and Critical Mass Theory, this study employs panel data regression analysis on 80 firm-year observations. The findings reveal that nationality diversity (β = 0.932, p < 0.001) and sustainability committee presence (β = 0.118, p = 0.013) have significant positive effects on carbon emission disclosure. However, gender diversity (p = 0.859) and environmental performance measured by the PROPER rating (p = 0.099) show no significant influence. The model explains 59.1% of the variance in carbon emission disclosure (Adjusted R² = 0.591). This research contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging economy context and offers practical implications for corporate governance policies in Indonesia.

title: Bureau-specific spatiotemporal carbon footprints and decarbonization pathways of China’s railways
source: iScience
summary: China's industrialization and urbanization have driven differentiated railway development across regions, necessitating refined carbon footprint (CF) accounting at the bureau scale to address spatiotemporal heterogeneity beyond national-lev
content: China's industrialization and urbanization have driven differentiated railway development across regions, necessitating refined carbon footprint (CF) accounting at the bureau scale to address spatiotemporal heterogeneity beyond national-level analysis. Here we developed a bureau-specific CF model incorporating energy mix, technological efficiency, fleet structure, and transport capacity, paired with driver and efficiency identification models. Results show China's operational railway emissions dropped 25.5% during 2010–2022 but concentrated in northern bureaus, with Taiyuan (2.78 Mt CO 2 -eq), Shenyang (2.75 Mt CO 2 -eq), and Zhengzhou (2.52 Mt CO 2 -eq) as top emitters in 2022, primarily driven by energy intensity and transport volume variations. Electrification reduced emission intensity (electric locomotives outperforming diesel ones) but relies on low-carbon electricity. Emission efficiency improved alongside declining emissions, with Taiyuan railway bureau ranked first in both total CF and efficiency. These findings emphasize region-specific decarbonization strategies integrating renewable energy, technological upgrading, and operational optimization.

title: Occupational exposures and worker health in decarbonization of energy-intensive industries: a scoping review protocol
source: Frontiers in Public Health
summary: Energy-intensive industries account for a substantial share of the global greenhouse gas emissions. The transition to net-zero emissions by 2050 demands development of industrial infrastructure and implementation of low-carbon technologies.
content: Energy-intensive industries account for a substantial share of the global greenhouse gas emissions. The transition to net-zero emissions by 2050 demands development of industrial infrastructure and implementation of low-carbon technologies. This transition is expected to result in altered exposure scenarios for workers. This scoping review aims to map the evidence on the occupational exposures and related health consequences of industrial decarbonization processes and to identify current research gaps. The review will follow the JBI and PRISMA-ScR guidelines for scoping reviews and is registered under the Open Science Framework (osf.io/7xzy4). A systematic literature search combining terms related to industrial decarbonization with occupational and worker-related terms will be conducted in Web of Science, Embase, MEDLINE, and Scopus. The search will be supplemented by targeted gray literature searches to identify relevant technical reports and policy documents. Data will be charted using a standardized template and synthesized descriptively and thematically by occupational exposure and health effects, investigated populations, industrial sectors, decarbonization processes or technologies to map patterns in the available evidence, identify emerging occupational risks, and current research gaps. Clinical trial registration osf.io/7xzy4 .

title: Carbon price and the misallocation of enterprise innovation resources
source: Applied Economics
summary: The carbon emissions trading mechanism increases production costs for regulated firms, which undoubtedly encourages enterprises to participate in technology research and development (R&D). However, it is unclear whether the carbon price wil
content: The carbon emissions trading mechanism increases production costs for regulated firms, which undoubtedly encourages enterprises to participate in technology research and development (R&D). However, it is unclear whether the carbon price will lead to misallocation of firms’ innovation resources. When R&D labour and capital are misallocated, increased R&D spending does not necessarily translate into innovation gains. Therefore, focusing on China’s carbon emissions trading mechanism, we systematically examine whether the carbon price affects firms’ innovation resource allocation and further evaluate social welfare after correcting for such misallocation. The analysis indicates that the carbon price exerts an inverted U-shaped effect on both R&D capital and labour misallocation; beyond a certain threshold, the carbon price helps reduce R&D resource misallocation. Further analysis indicates that correcting these misallocations significantly enhances both the quantity and quality of innovation output. These findings expand the research on carbon price mechanisms, highlight the importance of innovation resource allocation efficiency in climate governance, and provide evidence for designing carbon price policies that balance emission reduction targets with innovation efficiency.

title: ExoGarden: 3D-Printed Modular Eco-Habitats for Earth and Space
source: Research Directions Biotechnology Design
summary: Abstract Modern construction is a major driver of environmental harm and global carbon emissions. ExoGarden is an architectural prototype that reframes cultivation as infrastructure: a modular system for rapid, local growth of edible plants
content: Abstract Modern construction is a major driver of environmental harm and global carbon emissions. ExoGarden is an architectural prototype that reframes cultivation as infrastructure: a modular system for rapid, local growth of edible plants under strict resource constraints. Drawing on space-farming research and bioregenerative life-support principles, it explores closed-loopinspired cultivation in which nutrients and organic “waste” become inputs—supporting food production while reducing dependency on external supply chains. ExoGarden is designed for remote, resource-deprived, or climate-stressed contexts on Earth and in space, and proposes environmental remediation as an architectural function rather than an added feature. This pictorial communicates the project’s formal language, system logic, and exhibition-based prototyping through speculative scenarios, renders, and installation elements, outlining a life-promoting strategy where shelter, food, and ecology are co-designed. Originating as a master’s dissertation, ExoGarden received the Bio Art and Design Award in 2023 and was developed into an installation at MU Hybrid Art House.

title: Effect of barium titanate nanoparticles on pore architecture and early-stage chondrocyte response in breath figure–derived PLDLA scaffolds
source: Next Materials
summary: A suitable microenvironment is essential for chondrocytes to maintain their phenotype and extracellular matrix (ECM) production during long-term in vitro culture. Pore structure, interconnectivity, and the ability to provide natural cellula
content: A suitable microenvironment is essential for chondrocytes to maintain their phenotype and extracellular matrix (ECM) production during long-term in vitro culture. Pore structure, interconnectivity, and the ability to provide natural cellular cues are important properties in the scaffolds. Additionally, piezoelectric materials such as barium titanate can provide electromechanical stimulation to influence cellular behaviour. This study investigated the effect of the barium titanate nanoparticles (BTNP) on pore formation in poly-L/ D -lactide copolymer (PLDLA) scaffolds fabricated using the breath figure method. The final nanoparticle content, pore structure, and interconnectivity were characterised. Human articular chondrocytes were cultured on the scaffolds for two weeks to evaluate cytotoxicity, cell proliferation, cell morphology, and ECM production. The micropatterned porous structure was maintained across all PLDLA/BTNP scaffolds (BTNP content: 0, 10, 20, 30, and 40 wt%). X-ray microtomography (XRM) was able provided insight into pore structure and interconnectivity of the scaffolds. Pore diameter increased in the PLDLA/BTNP scaffold to approximately 20 µm, while in the PLDLA scaffolds, it was 2 µm. All PLDLA/BTNP scaffolds were non-cytotoxic, and cells were more spherical in the PLDLA/BTNP scaffolds, but there was no difference in ECM production. Overall, the amount of BTNPs influenced the scaffold structure. These early-stage findings demonstrated that scaffolds were non-cytotoxic and exhibited a porous architecture conducive to cell growth and maintenance. These findings highlight the potential of the developed PLDLA/BTNP scaffolds as three-dimensional platforms for long-term in vitro studies, enabling the investigation of cellular behaviour and cell–material interactions under physiologically relevant conditions.

title: Low-Carbon Emission Models for Hospitals and Pharmaceutical Industries for a Clean and Green Environment
source: OpenAlex 学术文献
summary: Climate change is a critical issue that calls for a detailed evaluation of carbon emissions in the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors. These industries contribute to the emission of greenhouse gases due to their high consumption of energ
content: Climate change is a critical issue that calls for a detailed evaluation of carbon emissions in the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors. These industries contribute to the emission of greenhouse gases due to their high consumption of energy and generation of waste. This chapter presents low-carbon emission models specific to various industries with the vision of establishing green and sustainable environments. The models give a lot of emphasis to energy efficiency, incorporating renewable energy, minimization of waste, and taking part in sustainable practices. In the matter of increased hospital efficiency, the authors recommend optimizing heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems, replacing traditional lighting with energy-efficient lighting, using renewable energy resources, and installing cogeneration systems. Installing waste management programs, including recycling and proper medical waste disposal, is also recommended. The use of green chemistry principles and life cycle assessment techniques, combined with continuous manufacturing and energy-efficient equipment, will be advantageous for the pharmaceutical industry. Adoption of these measures will automatically reduce carbon emissions, fight the burgeoning problem of climate change, and ensure a sustainable future. Collaboration among government officials, pharma industry stakeholders, and researchers is essential for the development of these models.

title: Microbially Precipitated Calcite Encapsulated Biochar for MICP Soil Improvement
source: Figshare
summary: Microbially Induced Carbonate Precipitation (MICP) leverages bacterial activity to create conditions favorable for calcium carbonate precipitation. Through the introduction of ureolytic bacteria, urea and a suitable calcium source into soil
content: Microbially Induced Carbonate Precipitation (MICP) leverages bacterial activity to create conditions favorable for calcium carbonate precipitation. Through the introduction of ureolytic bacteria, urea and a suitable calcium source into soil, calcium carbonate precipitates form cementing bonds between soil particles, increasing soil strength and stiffness. This process has demonstrated significant potential as a sustainable alternative to traditional soil improvement techniques, lowering carbon emissions and secondary environmental impacts. However, its treatment longevity and efficacy remain limited as bacterial activity decreases over time. To address these challenges, this research explores the use of biochar as an additive to enhance MICP performance. The study investigates whether biochar can be uniformly encapsulated within microbially precipitated calcite to improve treatment resilience, thereby extending and enhancing the performance of existing MICP soil treatments.

title: Bio‐Based Piezoresistive Composites for Sustainable Sensing: Advances Toward Circular Economy Systems
source: Journal of Polymer Science
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid proliferation of electronic waste has sparked interest in bio‐based piezoresistive composites for sustainable sensing applications. This study connects materials science with circular‐economy principles to design, produce
content: ABSTRACT The rapid proliferation of electronic waste has sparked interest in bio‐based piezoresistive composites for sustainable sensing applications. This study connects materials science with circular‐economy principles to design, produce, and implement environmentally sustainable sensors. Bio‐derived feedstocks, such as cellulose, chitosan, alginate, and agricultural residues, substitute petroleum‐derived resources and facilitate regenerative product lifecycles. The combination of natural fibers, bio‐sourced conductive fillers, and sophisticated polymer matrices results in enhanced sensitivity, durability, biodegradability, and recyclability, with reduced carbon emissions. Sustainable processing methods and material tactics such as microstructural tailoring, interfacial engineering, and hierarchical structures improve performance. Exemplified applications encompass wearable health monitoring, intelligent textiles, structural health assessment, and environmental sensing. Life‐cycle assessments indicate reductions in global warming potential and enhanced circularity with feasible end‐of‐life solutions. Significant hurdles persist in aligning performance with traditional sensors, standardizing evaluations, and scaling manufacturing. Future directions highlight AI‐driven materials optimization, self‐healing capabilities, multifunctional designs, and alignment between policy and industry. The paper also consolidates advancements and provides a framework for the use of bio‐based piezoresistive composites in sustainable electronics.

title: Beware of the “decoupling trap”: identification, evolution, and driving factors of real and pseudo decoupling in China's city-level building sector
source: Engineering Construction & Architectural Management
summary: Purpose Cities and industries trapped in a “decoupling trap” risk compromising their own, provincial, and even national decoupling progress and dual-carbon targets. As one of the three major emission sources, the building sector’s carbon em
content: Purpose Cities and industries trapped in a “decoupling trap” risk compromising their own, provincial, and even national decoupling progress and dual-carbon targets. As one of the three major emission sources, the building sector’s carbon emissions are of particular significance in this context. Design/methodology/approach Employing conventional decoupling analysis, an auxiliary “decoupling trap” diagnostic lens, and Geo-detector methods, this research examines whether apparent emissions–output decoupling in the building sector is internally supported by changes in energy intensity and carbon intensity, using panel data from 290 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2005 to 2022. A driver analysis framework further quantifies the individual and interactive factor impacts of factors on genuine versus spurious decoupling states. Findings In China's city-level building sector, the main findings are as follows: (1) After applying the auxiliary trap-related diagnostic lens, over half of the cities show intensity-mismatch or pseudo-decoupling states, while more internally consistent decoupling is mainly found in central, western, and northeastern regions; (2) the geographic center of true decoupling has shifted westward and southward, with over 90% of truly decoupled cities belonging to middle- and high-income groups; and (3) true decoupling is more often associated with joint endogenous structural conditions and external support, with policy-related variables depending on cities' internal foundations. Originality/value These findings demonstrate the value of using a trap-related diagnostic lens as a complement to conventional decoupling analysis, helping distinguish apparent emissions–output decoupling from more internally consistent decarbonization patterns and providing empirical support for differentiated urban mitigation policies.

title: Perspective of Student Commuters on Electric Vehicle Transportation: A Convergent-Parallel Approach
source: American Journal of Environment and Climate
summary: This study employed a convergent-parallel mixed-methods approach to explore student commuters’ perspectives on electric vehicle (EV) transportation in Davao City, Philippines. The research integrated quantitative data from 298 survey respon
content: This study employed a convergent-parallel mixed-methods approach to explore student commuters’ perspectives on electric vehicle (EV) transportation in Davao City, Philippines. The research integrated quantitative data from 298 survey respondents and qualitative insights from in-depth interviews and a focus group discussion with 15 participants. Quantitative findings showed a generally positive perception of e-vehicles, particularly regarding environmental concern, attitude, and perceived safety. However, infrastructure and affordability were areas of concern. Qualitative results expanded these findings, revealing issues such as inconsistent government support, lack of charging stations, safety concerns due to unregistered e-vehicles, and varying affordability experiences. Despite these challenges, students expressed strong support for sustainable transportation and were optimistic about e-vehicle adoption, provided improvements are made in infrastructure, policy support, and technology. The study contributes to the understanding of e-vehicle acceptance among young commuters and offers insights for policymakers aiming to promote environmentally friendly urban mobility in alignment with sustainable development goals.

title: Contractual and relational governance in high-standard farmland management: evidence from hunan province, China
source: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
summary: As a key influencing factor of governance effectiveness, sound organizational operations in practice are largely attributable to the application of appropriate governance mechanisms. Based on transaction cost theory and using 442 micro-leve
content: As a key influencing factor of governance effectiveness, sound organizational operations in practice are largely attributable to the application of appropriate governance mechanisms. Based on transaction cost theory and using 442 micro-level survey data from China's Hunan Province as samples, this study employs structural equation modeling to analyze the impact of contractual and relational governance mechanisms on the performance of high-standard farmland management. The results indicate: (1) The governance performance of high-standard farmland is enhanced through the complementary effects of both contractual and relational governance mechanisms. Each mechanism exerts a direct, positive influence on performance outcomes; (2) Contractual governance contributes more significantly than relational governance to the improvement of governance performance; (3) The impact of contractual governance on the governance performance of high-standard farmland is partially mediated by relational governance. Accordingly, it is recommended to refine governance mechanisms in a context-specific manner, implement tailored policies for contractual and relational governance, appropriately and timely guide contractual governance, and promote integrated governance approaches to leverage the complementary strengths of both mechanisms.

title: A Review of Electric Vehicle Integration in Peer–to–Peer Energy Networks
source: World Electric Vehicle Journal
summary: The rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) adoption presents significant challenges for power system stability while creating new opportunities for decentralized energy management. Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy networks have emerged as a promisi
content: The rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) adoption presents significant challenges for power system stability while creating new opportunities for decentralized energy management. Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy networks have emerged as a promising approach for transforming EVs from passive loads into coordinated grid assets. This paper presents a comprehensive review of EV-P2P integration through a three-layer architectural framework that systematically connects physical infrastructure, market mechanisms, and intelligent control strategies. The Physical Layer reviews how V2X technologies and bidirectional charging enable EVs to operate as flexible storage resources and ancillary service providers. The Transactional Layer reviews on blockchain-based platforms, auction mechanisms, and game-theoretic models for secure energy trading. The Intelligence Layer reviews advanced control strategies, including decentralized optimization methods such as the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Collectively, the reviewed studies demonstrate that these approaches enable EVs to operate as flexible loads, distributed storage resources, and ancillary service providers, while improving energy trading efficiency, reducing operating costs, and alleviating network congestion under simulated operating conditions. Despite these promising results, a substantial gap remains between simulation-based studies and practical implementation. Future research should prioritize integrated pilot projects to evaluate scalability, interoperability, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance under realistic operating conditions.

title: Intensification of cocoa production and biodiversity in Cameroon
source: Discover Environment
summary: Cocoa cultivation is economically vital for Cameroon, the world’s sixth-largest producer, but agricultural intensification threatens biodiversity. While previous research has examined cocoa expansion impacts, few studies have quantified how
content: Cocoa cultivation is economically vital for Cameroon, the world’s sixth-largest producer, but agricultural intensification threatens biodiversity. While previous research has examined cocoa expansion impacts, few studies have quantified how yield intensification affects threatened species populations. This study evaluates the effects of cocoa production intensification on biodiversity in Cameroon using an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model applied to data from 1992 to 2022. Intensification is measured by cocoa yield (kg/ha), while biodiversity is assessed through IUCN Red List counts of threatened mammals, birds, reptiles, and plants taxonomic groups ecologically relevant to cocoa-growing regions. Results indicate that increased yields have significant negative effects on biodiversity, particularly long-term impacts on mammals (coefficient: 0.0142) and reptiles (coefficient: 0.0021). Short-term effects were observed for mammals, reptiles, and plants. These positive coefficients indicate that higher yields correspond to more threatened species, reflecting biodiversity degradation likely driven by increased chemical inputs and habitat modification. Findings highlight the need for sustainable agricultural practices limiting agrochemical use and favoring ecosystem conservation in cocoa farming systems.

title: Metrics for Implementing and Assessing the Environmental Impact of Healthcare and Other Products
source: OpenAlex 学术文献
summary: Strong matrices to analyse a product’s environmental impact are becoming more important as healthcare and other businesses recognise the need for ecological sustainability. These matrices improve public health by reducing environmental burd
content: Strong matrices to analyse a product’s environmental impact are becoming more important as healthcare and other businesses recognise the need for ecological sustainability. These matrices improve public health by reducing environmental burden and carbon footprint. Life cycle evaluations, green chemistry-based manufacturing procedures, and green engineering have been considered to analyse the impact. This approach involves extensive scientific studies to identify and quantify the possible harm that drugs may bring to land and aquatic ecosystems. A life cycle assessment assesses toxicity, resource depletion, climate change, and health impacts. Environmental performance benchmarks, including greenhouse gas emissions, waste production, and resource depletion, are used for improvement. These matrices can be used in normal agencies to boost use. This will spur sustainable product innovations. The results showed three views and dynamics that are altering actor roles and speeding up the socio-technical transition to a state based on distributed dynamic network collaboration. The chosen transition techniques emphasise innovation, information sharing, and stakeholder participation from local to global. The framework for studying the transition to sustainable healthcare and its effects is provided.

title: The sustainability paradox in urban food tourism: dissonance, control, and moral disengagement among Gen Z
source: Sustainability Science Practice and Policy
summary: Urban food tourism intersects with sustainability agendas, yet informal street-food ecosystems often lack visible environmental practices, creating governance and behavior-formation challenges for pro-sustainability cohorts such as Generati
content: Urban food tourism intersects with sustainability agendas, yet informal street-food ecosystems often lack visible environmental practices, creating governance and behavior-formation challenges for pro-sustainability cohorts such as Generation Z (Gen Z). This study examines how unsustainable environmental cues in these settings shape Gen Z tourists’ sustainable street-food consumption intentions. Grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the model specifies cognitive dissonance, sustainability-related moral disengagement, and perceived behavioral control as mechanisms through which sustainability-scarce environments condition intentions. Survey data from Gen Z visitors to Bangkok’s street-food districts were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling, complemented by K-means segmentation and multi-group comparisons. Perceived unsustainable cues are associated with higher cognitive dissonance and stronger perceived behavioral control; both mechanisms show positive associations with sustainable consumption intention, whereas moral disengagement shows a negative association. These positive associations are stronger among a high-awareness segment, while the negative disengagement–intention association remains comparatively stable across segments. The findings extend S-O-R logic to informal food systems where sustainability signals are weak, showing that problem salience can coincide with stronger efficacy perceptions when actionable remedies are salient—a counterintuitive finding that challenges standard TPB predictions about constrained environments. Practically, the results support interventions that increase perceived control at the point of choice, including deposit-return infrastructure, eco-zoned vendor clusters, and bring-your-own incentives, while constraining justificatory space through accountability and norm cues. Overall, the study offers SDG 12-aligned guidance for destinations seeking to preserve street-food livelihoods and cultural vibrancy while accelerating waste-reduction transitions.

title: Utilization of fleet management system for performance analysis and CO2 emissions during skidding operations in Western Carpathians
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Introduction Gathering and analyzing the operational parameter information from the timber extraction operation enables to study the impact of several factors on machine productivity, fuel consumption, and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions.
content: Introduction Gathering and analyzing the operational parameter information from the timber extraction operation enables to study the impact of several factors on machine productivity, fuel consumption, and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. One option is to use fleet management system (FMS), which is recording continuously various types of data resources and providing thereby a large amount of data on major operational parameters and GNSS location of machines. Methods The operational parameter data from FMS of two skidders (HSM model 805HD and LKT model 81 ITL) were utilized for comparison study. The data covered a period of 1,605 working days, during which was recorded 316,916 records about machine GNSS locations, operations performed, and fuel consumption for analysis. The Mann–Whitney U test and generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) were used for data analysis. Results The results showed that the average productivity of skidding operations for HSM were 5.95 m 3 PMH −1 and 5.20 m 3 SMH −1 and LKT were 5.12 m 3 PMH −1 and 4.16 m 3 SMH −1 . Total fuel consumption per working shift was significantly affected by the number of productive machine hours (PMH) worked and the distance traveled (R 2 m = 0.416). The average fuel consumption for HSM and LKT skidders were 1.03 and 1.34 L m −3 , respectively. Furthermore, CO 2 emissions for HSM and LKT were 2.77 and 3.60 kg CO₂ m −3 , respectively. These values were about 30% higher for LKT than HSM skidder. GLMM analysis confirmed that 38.9% of the variability in the kg CO 2 of PMH −1 emission values were influenced by the specific operation being performed, while the influence of the skidder type, road type, and season were not significant. Conclusion The results provide valuable information on the impact of various factors on the productivity, fuel consumption, and CO₂ emissions of combined (winch and crane) timber skidding method when the FMS data was utilized.

title: Jute Bags as a Catalyst for Green Solutions
source: OpenAlex 学术文献
summary: Plastic bag waste is rapidly becoming a global concern these days. Plastic shopping bags have an extended environmental impact and consume a lot of resources. Jute bags provide an eco-friendly alternative since they are biodegradable, eco-f
content: Plastic bag waste is rapidly becoming a global concern these days. Plastic shopping bags have an extended environmental impact and consume a lot of resources. Jute bags provide an eco-friendly alternative since they are biodegradable, eco-friendly, and plant-based. Jute is an eco-friendly as it is a natural, biodegradable, and plant-based fiber. Among its ecological benefits, jute reduces carbon emissions while improving conditions for efficient waste management, just like the virtuous circle of a circular economy-that supports resource reutilization with minimal waste generation. It contributes to economic growth because it avails jobs to rural farmers. Even though jute bags have these advantages, they are not as strong as plastic, and farm labor-based practices can easily give way to exploitations. Innovations, in farming and production, made jute more viable, with more efficient and automated manufactures making jute products more available and competitive.

title: Enhancing legal collaborative governance for cross-border marine pollution in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area: aligning rules, transforming mechanisms, and coordinating institutions
source: Frontiers in Marine Science
summary: Within the framework of “One Country, Two Systems and Three Legal Jurisdictions,” managing cross-regional marine pollution in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area encounters significant legal obstacles, including inconsistent regu
content: Within the framework of “One Country, Two Systems and Three Legal Jurisdictions,” managing cross-regional marine pollution in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area encounters significant legal obstacles, including inconsistent regulations, differing standards, and unclear liability determination. Current models of administrative agreements and soft law collaboration lack stability and universal binding force, hindering effective responses to the challenges posed by the transboundary nature of marine pollution. This study utilizes methodologies from legal hermeneutics, comparative law, and case analysis methodologies, focusing on two illustrative cases—the Yachong River in Zhuhai-Macau and Dapeng Bay in Shenzhen-Hong Kong. Through this analysis, we systematically explore key issues within the legal frameworks, governance mechanisms, liability assignment, and remediation measures across these three regions.
